newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks race ahead, Bombay at 52-week high.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks race ahead, Bombay at 52-week high.

text.p: ** (1245 GMT) - Indian shares close off day's highs, but
end with sharp gains over previous day on fund buying
** Bombay's benchmark index closes 47.04 points, or 1.18
percent, higher at 4,029.99, off a new 52-week high of
4065.0 reached during mid-session
** Delhi index up 10.90 pts at 849.04, Calcutta gains 0.81
pts at 114.90 and Madras 77.02 pts at 4,038.08
** Truckmaker TELCO, tobacco firm ITC and telecom stock
MTNL among key gainers on Friday
** India's ruling United Front coalition says no meeting on
Sunday to decide on oil price hike
Indian shares ended off a blistering blue-chip led-rally on Fridya, as speculators booked profits near close, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index surpassed a 52-week high of 4,029.56 set in March this year, with multinational stocks and state-run firms leading the uptrend, players said.
Postponement of a crucial meeting of the decision-making panel of India's ruling United Front scheduled for Sunday gave an impetus to players to create fresh positions.
The Bombay index which raced five percent this week is expected to power ahead at the start of new account on Monday.

"I don't see any big reaction till the index reaches the 4,200 level next week," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief trader at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs. "There has been a lot of fund buying that we have seen."

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have said they favour increases in petroleum product prices, while left parties in the coalition want alternatives to be considered.
A decision has been deferred several times already.
Traders said foreign funds and speculators were buyers in frontliners like ITC, MTNL, Tata Tea and TELCO.
"We have a year-end target of 4,500 for the Bombay index," said V.V.Sivakumar, head of reseach at Peregrine Capital. "We are still sticking with that though the markets are doing very well."
"This rally which we have seen over the past few days will probably run for some more days."
Shares of India's largest private sector firm Reliance Industries lagged in a sharp rally at the Bombay exchange.
Reliance fell one rupee to 319.50 at the Bombay Stock Exchange amid volumes of over 5.59 million shares.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
